about_page_description: Game audio designer with a background in music, maths, physics, and technical implementation across game engines and immersive training.
hook: I build game audio from both sides: creative and technical.
intro_sub: Belgium · DAE Howest · Technical sound design · XR Labs
story_1: Gaming was my first passion, and over time it turned into a real drive to learn game development. Before that, I was already deeply into making music, which is what naturally pulled me toward audio in games.
story_2: My background in maths and physics gave me a strong instinct for technical learning. That pushed me toward programming, systems thinking, and the more exact side of solving creative problems.
story_3: Three years at DAE in Kortrijk, one of the strongest game development schools in Europe, gave me a foundation in C++, C#, audio implementation in Unity and Unreal, and everyday work with middleware.
background_1: At some point, just playing games stopped being enough. I wanted to understand how games are built, what makes them work, and how different disciplines come together in one experience.
background_2: Before I got serious about game development, I was already deeply into music. That is what pulled me toward game audio in the first place, while maths and physics gave me the mindset to enjoy the more technical side of implementation.
background_3: At DAE I spent three years learning the foundations of C++, C#, Unity, Unreal, middleware, and collaborative production. The student projects there made me want not only to work on games, but to keep building, shipping, and sharing that work with other people.
approach_1: Since February, I have been interning at XR Labs as the lead technical sound designer. I design sounds, implement them, and keep working on them until they feel right inside the project rather than in isolation.
approach_2: What I like most about that work is that it is not abstract. I get to collaborate on training simulations for police, military, and customs units, then see those scenarios tested, hear the feedback, and understand what actually helps realism and what does not.
approach_3: That is why I keep focusing on both sound quality and believable acoustics. A lot of my work goes into Steam Audio reflections, sound transmission, material absorption, and the small details that make a VR or AR training simulation feel convincing.
cta_text: Game audio, technical sound design, implementation, tools, or immersive audio work. If you have a project, I'm happy to talk.
